title: Protocol for the isolation and culture of mouse dorsal root ganglion neurons for imaging applications
protocol: Sacrifice the animal with CO₂.
Alternatively, anesthetize the animal with 5% isoflurane.
Once deeply anesthetized, sacrifice the animal via decapitation.
Decapitate the animal with large surgical scissors, cutting as close to the base of the skull as possible.
Spray the animal thoroughly with 70% ethanol.
Pinch the skin above the pelvis with forceps and lift.
Using fine dissecting scissors, cut the pinched skin beginning at the pelvis and continuing in a cranial direction to remove the dorsal skin.
Cut the tissue between the scapulae and upper ribs.
Pull the scapulae away from the vertebral column.
Cut the vertebral column at or below the lumbosacral joint.
Use the thumb and index finger to locate the top of the pelvis.
Insert the blade of the fine scissors under the ventral side of the pelvis perpendicular to the vertebral column, with the other blade remaining exposed on the dorsal side.
Squeeze firmly to cut through the upper region of the pelvis.
Cut in a cranial direction through the ribs on the left and right side of the spine.
Lift the vertebral column and cut any tissue and organs attached to the ventral side.
Use fine scissors to cut away any muscle and fatty tissue obscuring the dorsal and ventral sides of the vertebral column.
Remove enough tissue that the midline of the vertebrae can be seen along the entire length of the vertebral column on both the dorsal and ventral sides.
Insert the bottom blade of a fine dissecting scissors into the opening on the cervical end of the spine and cut in a sacral direction along the dorsal midline down the length of the spine.
Repeat the process for the ventral side of the spine.
Store hemi-sections in ice-cold HBSS.
Harvest DRG from one hemi-section at a time, leaving the other submerged in ice-cold HBSS.
Remove the spinal cord from the hemi-section with fine forceps.
Gently insert one prong of the forceps between the spinal cord and interior of the vertebrae.
Lift or peel the spinal cord away from the bone.
Do not pull with too much force, as you may remove DRGs with the spinal cord.
Locate the intervertebral foramen between the vertebrae.
Insert the tip of a fine forceps into the space beside the DRG, slightly open.
Maneuver the tip of the forceps under the “head” of the DRG.
Gently close the forceps and lift out the DRG.
Place the removed DRG in a petri dish containing PBS or HBSS.
Cut the fibers from the DRG “head” using fine spring scissors.
Place the cut DRG in the collection tube.
Keep the collected DRG on ice for the duration of the dissection.
Submerge the hemi-section in ice-cold HBSS periodically during harvesting to prevent tissue drying out.
Apply cold HBSS with a dropper periodically during DRG harvesting if necessary.
Keep fur soaked in 70% ethanol to avoid fungal contamination of the culture.
Change gloves and move to a new work area once the vertebral column has been isolated.
Pellet the DRG by centrifuging for 1–2 min at 400 × g.
Thaw aliquots of Solutions A, D, and T while centrifuging.
Warm media in a 37°C water bath.
Aspirate the HBSS carefully without disrupting the pellet.
Add 1 ml of Solution A to the vial.
Pipette with modest force to break up the pellet.
Tap the vial gently if needed to further disrupt the pellet.
Avoid aggressive handling to prevent tissues from sticking to the sidewall of the vial.
Incubate for 10–25 min at 37°C, tapping to disrupt the pellet halfway through the incubation time.
Centrifuge for 1–2 min at 400 × g.
Aspirate Solution A.
Add 1 mL Solution D.
Tap the tube to disrupt the pellet.
Incubate for 20 min at 37°C, tapping to disrupt the pellet halfway through the incubation time.
During this incubation, aspirate the PDL solution from the coated culture dish and wash once with sterile ddH2O.
Aspirate and allow to dry in a BSC.
Centrifuge for 1–2 min at 400 × g.
Aspirate Solution D.
Add 1 mL of Solution T.
Triturate using a P1000 until homogenous.
Place a 70 μm cell strainer in an open 50 mL conical vial such that the strainer basket sits inside the opening of the conical vial.
Pipette the mixture over the strainer.
Wash the strainer with 10–20 mL of warmed DMEM/F12.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 400 × g.
Aspirate the media.
Resuspend in an appropriate volume of DRG culture media.
Resuspend cells in media to plate as a single droplet per well.
Use 25–30 μL of cell suspension for ∼5,000 cells.
Pipette the desired volume of cell suspension onto the culture dish or cover slip.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 30–45 min to allow cells to adhere.
Gently add an appropriate volume of media after incubation.
Completely replace the media every other day without washing off the cells.
Monitor cell morphology over time with a phase contrast microscope.
Ensure neurons are visible and identifiable by their large circular soma after the first media change.
Observe neurites growing within hours on all neurons within a day.
Aspirate the media from each well.
Wash with PBS warmed to 37°C.
Incubate for 2–5 minutes after adding PBS.
Repeat this for 3 total PBS washes.
Aspirate the PBS and add 4% formaldehyde.
Incubate for 15 min.
Aspirate and add PBS.
Perform 3 PBS washes as in step 21.
Aspirate the PBS and add 0.5% Triton X-100.
Incubate for 10 minutes.
Aspirate the PBS and add blocking solution (10% goat serum in PBS).
Incubate for 1 hour.
Aspirate primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution.
Add primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution.
Incubate at 4°C for 14–18 hours.
Perform 3 PBS washes.
Aspirate secondary antibodies diluted in blocking solution.
Add secondary antibodies diluted in blocking solution.
Incubate for 1 hour away from light.
Perform 3 PBS washes.
Aspirate PBS.
Separate the wells from the slide if using chamber slides.
Place the slide in the plastic frame with the tab at the open end.
Position the splitter in the channels of the frame.
Press the splitter forward to remove the wells, lifting slightly at the back.
Remove the slide and splitter from the frame.
Lift the wells off of the slide.
Add 80–90 μL mounting media to the slide in evenly dispersed drops.
Place a coverslip on the slide.
Press down gently with the back of a P200 pipette tip or capped pen to force any air bubbles out from under the cover slip.
Wick away excess mounting media from the edges of the coverslip using a paper towel frequently enough to prevent beads forming.
Allow the mounting media to set for roughly 2 h at 20°C–23°C if using hard mount media such as ProLong.
Seal the edges of the slide with quick drying nail polish, taking care not to obscure any part of the viewable area.
Ensure that nail polish has completely dried before imaging.
Store slides properly if not imaging the same day, considering fluorophore stability and storage conditions.
If storing longer than 48 hours, store slides at -20°C.
For optimal preservation of fluorescence, ensure proper mounting media and light exposure conditions are used during storage.
Critical: Always perform all experimental conditions and controls for a replicate in parallel.
Always image replicates on the same day to maintain consistency in quantifications.
Use the chosen cell-type marker to set a region of interest (ROI) when collecting immunofluorescence data.
